messages:
lina: quick ping 1 — discovered a goroutine that never exits in the Go generator when the ctx used to construct it is cancelled mid-handshake. affects our generator sample that does a short auth refresh timeout.
aj: can you drop the minimal code that reproduces? which SDK release?
lina: vendored v0.13.2. minimal snippet:
```
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 30*time.Millisecond)
gen, err := client.NewGenerator(ctx, modelID, opts...)
// we then immediately call gen.Next() or gen.Stream()
```
when ctx cancels during the initial handshake the constructor returns error but there's still a goroutine reading from the connection.
ryan: that's consistent with start-up ordering where the reader goroutine is started before we know the handshake succeeded. if constructor returns early, the goroutine lacks a stop signal.
aj: simple guard: defer starting the reader until handshake future resolves successfully. also add a select on ctx.Done() in constructor so we bail early without starting anything.
lina: tried both: delaying goroutine spawn until after handshake fixes it locally. adding the ctx.Done() check in constructor also prevents the hang.
ryan: we'll need a unit test that simulates slow handshake + cancelled ctx to prevent regression. add a subtest that constructs with a cancelling ctx and asserts no goroutines leak after timeout.
aj: docs note: clarify that current constructor uses the passed ctx for handshake; other SDKs (py/js) handle this differently. we should be explicit whether ctx controls generator lifetime vs handshake only.
lina: my preference: ship the non-breaking guard now (delay reader + test) and follow-up with an API fairness RFC if we want separate lifecycle ctx.
ryan: agreed. open a PR with title "go: guard generator reader on handshake completion (fix leak)" and tag me + aj. post links to eng-runtime and devex channels.

lina: PR incoming in ~30m with test and minimal fix. thanks all. :raised_hands:
